conventions.convention: The concentration function uses the full squared RKHS norm, strict approximation balls, and the negative logarithm of the centered strict small-ball probability.
Hellinger distance has normalization h²(P,Q)=∫(√p−√q)², with no factor 1/2.
Local KL bounds use the direction KL(P₀∥Pθ). The denominator proof requires second moments of log likelihood ratios, rather than squared first moments.
Binary regression uses joint densities relative to G times counting measure; their density L² distance equals √2 times the L²(G) distance between response probabilities.
The unknown parameter σ is standard deviation. Its independent prior has a Lebesgue density bounded below on a fixed positive compact interval containing σ₀, including possible endpoints.
The universal fixed-design rate is max{εₙ,√(log n/n)}. The sharper εₙ rate requires a nonzero Gaussian law or, for the zero law, a locally upper-bounded scale density.

Gaussian priors are tight Borel Banach-valued laws, with explicit jointly measurable model densities or evaluation versions; cylinder-process specifications alone are insufficient. AC, countable choice and the stated relative Hahn–Banach premise are carried explicitly.

load_bearing.statement: Under its stated Gaussian concentration, measurability, truth-support and model hypotheses, sufficiently large fixed multiples of εₙ give expected posterior contraction in Hellinger distance for log-Gaussian densities and L²(G) response-probability distance for binary regression. Fixed-design Gaussian regression with the stated independent scale prior contracts in empirical-mean-plus-scale distance at ρₙ=max{εₙ,√(log n/n)}; εₙ replaces ρₙ for a nonzero Gaussian law, or for the zero law with a scale density bounded above near σ₀.

For the stated jointly measurable dominated independent-observation model, measurable Kₙ with Π(Kₙ)≥exp(−Cnεₙ²), average KL at most εₙ², and the displayed average E₀[log(pᵢθ/pᵢ₀)]² at most εₙ², Dₙ is finite almost surely and P₀⁽ⁿ⁾{Dₙ≥exp(−(C+2)nεₙ²)}≥1−1/(nεₙ²).

A denominator lower bound with exponent A holding in probability, sieve-tail exponent B>A, and null and uniform sieve-alternative test-error exponent T>A imply posterior mass of the tested alternative tends to zero in P₀,n-probability, provided nεₙ²→∞.

For the stated fixed design and compact positive scale interval, a measurable function sieve covered at supremum radius 3εₙ by at most exp(6Cnεₙ²) centers admits, for every T>0 and sufficiently large fixed M, null and uniform alternative errors at most exp(−Tnεₙ²) outside empirical-mean-plus-scale distance Mεₙ, for all sufficiently large n.

For the stated independent standard normals, the linear statistic has tail at most 2exp(−nt²/(2σ²‖c‖ₙ²)), with zero probability when ‖c‖ₙ=0. If ‖δ‖ₙ≤1 and 0<t≤b²+2, the centered residual-energy statistic has tail at most 2exp(−nt²/(4V_b)), where V_b=2b⁴+4b².
A continuous Gaussian direction ℓ with variance τ²>0 gives φ_w₀(ε)≥log(1/ε)−log(2‖ℓ‖/(√(2π)τ)) for every ε>0, with the stated nonnegative Hilbert approximation penalty.

A tight centered Borel Gaussian law on a real Banach space is carried by a separable closed linear subspace E; its restricted law is tight and centered Gaussian, and its support in E equals its ambient support.

concerns.concern: The Statement writes E_{i0}[log(p_iθ(Y_i)/p_i0(Y_i))]^2, placing the square outside the expectation brackets. Literally this bounds the squared mean, whereas proof 1.2 requires E_{i0}[(log(p_iθ/p_i0))²]. The written claim is false: take n=100, εₙ=1, C=1, a singleton prior, and IID observations on {0,1}. Let P₀(1)=q=0.0005 and Pθ(1)=q exp(−1000), with complementary masses at 0. Then KL(P₀∥Pθ)≈0.499500125 and the squared expected log ratio≈0.249500375, so both written bounds hold and prior mass is 1. If any observation equals 1, log Dₙ≤−1000+99[−log(1−q)]<−999, below the claimed threshold −300. This event has probability 1−(1−q)^100≈0.04878247, exceeding the allowed 0.01. The theorem's Gaussian application supplies the intended stronger second-moment condition, but this supplier Statement needs correction.

Proof 2.1 says, 'The same map W is Borel as an E-valued map' after establishing only μ(E)=1. W may take values outside E on a nonempty null event, so the same map need not have codomain E. Restricting to W⁻¹(E), or replacing W by 0 on its measurable null complement, closes the issue and preserves the law and subsequent argument.

seams_checked.note: The IID denominator and testing suppliers are used in the IID density and binary branches with their stated directional second-moment, joint-measurability and domination hypotheses. Cover-to-packing rescaling preserves the testing metric; the binary joint densities satisfy the required uniform bound by one.

The consumer preserves the full-squared RKHS concentration convention, separable tight Borel law, truth-support and choice assumptions. Its uses of the support, Gaussian expansion and sieve statements preserve their hypotheses and constants. The supplier page also correctly distinguishes prior concentration bounds from posterior contraction.
